01

Media Planner Agent

From a plan to published campaigns - one guided flow.

Media Plans takes a media plan and turns it into live-ready ad campaigns. You create a plan one of three ways, Carter imports it and tells you exactly what's missing or needs your attention, and then you review and publish, landing on the finished campaigns. That's the whole flow.

1. Three ways to create a plan
Start however suits you: build it with the agent - describe your plan in plain language and the Strategy Agent builds it out for you; upload an existing plan - bring your own CSV or XLSX file, with a template to start from if you need one; or import from your tools - connect Monday.com or Salesforce once, then pull a plan straight in. Whichever route you pick, it feeds into the same flow from there.
2. It imports everything and flags what needs you
Once your plan is in, Carter reads it and maps it to a structured campaign plan automatically. Then it's upfront with you: anything it had to assume, and anything still missing or needing your attention, is surfaced clearly. Fill in what's needed, let Carter suggest values, or just tell it what to change, and once nothing's outstanding, the plan is ready to build.
3. Review, publish, done
Carter builds the campaigns from your plan, and you review them before anything goes live - budget, channels, targeting, and creatives all editable. Approve what looks right, publish, and you land on your finished campaigns.
Why it matters Media planning usually means a spreadsheet and a slow hand-off before anything goes live. Media Planner collapses that, create a plan any way you like, let Carter structure it and tell you what it needs, then review and publish.

02

Events & Identity

One tag. One customer. One journey - online and offline.

Events & Identity pulls event collection, customer identity, and offline sales into a single system. One tag captures activity across web and app, every event ties back to one customer profile, and in-store purchases land in the same journey as everything online. One profile and everything hangs on it.

1. One tag. Zero upkeep.
Drop one lightweight tag in your site header. It knows each page type and fires the right events on its own, no per-page code. Adding a new channel later? No site changes needed. Events can flow straight from your server too, and Carter clears the duplicates, so a sale that arrives from both the browser and the server still counts exactly once.
2. One customer, everywhere.
The same shopper shows up looking like strangers, logged out here, signed in there, arriving from an ad. Events & Identity stitches those fragments into one profile. Confirmed signals lead the way - a login, a matched email or phone, a loyalty ID - with best-guess matches as a clearly ranked fallback, each carrying its own confidence score. Profiles hold across devices, survive a cookie wipe, and log every merge along the way.
3. Online-to-offline, closed.
In-store purchases are the most under-attributed conversions in retail, and Events & Identity finally brings them in. Point-of-sale transactions are securely imported and stitched to the same profile as online activity, so a sale at the counter lands in the customer's journey exactly like an online one, right alongside the touchpoints that led to it. Personal details like email and phone are pre-hashed by the retailer before they ever leave, so Carter never receives raw customer data.
Why it matters Events & Identity folds tracking, identity, and offline sales into one platform, capabilities that usually mean juggling separate, expensive third-party tools. For small and mid-sized agencies, that consolidation is real money saved.

03

Attribution & Value

Credit where it's earned - de-duplicated, and reconcilable.

Attribution & Value turns Carter's unified customer profile into a clear view of what actually drove each sale. Because every touchpoint is tied to one customer, credit is de-duplicated across channels, so you see one set of numbers instead of six platforms each claiming the same conversion. It comes in three parts: a configurable multi-touch attribution engine, de-duplicated reach and customer value, and a single timeline of every customer's journey.

1. Multi-Touch Attribution
Pick your model, set your rules, and let the credit land where it belongs. Choose Linear, Time Decay, or Data-Driven. Set click and impression lookback windows, then override them per channel, view-through for some, click-only for others. Every conversion is broken into one row per touchpoint, with credit adding up to exactly 1.0, from an engine that runs inside your own warehouse.

The headline is reconciliation. Carter shows its de-duplicated ROAS right next to the ROAS each channel claims for itself, and spells out the over-claim channel by channel, because platforms each take full credit for shared conversions. No black box - every run is versioned, with the exact configuration snapshotted behind it.

And there's depth underneath: the funnel from impressions to clicks to conversions, CAC and LTV by channel, spend and ROAS broken out by ad type and placement, your top converting paths, and per-customer results you can open right down to each touchpoint's credit.
2. Reach, LTV & Value
Because every impression is tied to one person, reach is de-duplicated across channels, the same shopper seen on Meta, The Trade Desk, and Search counts once, not three times. See gross reach against true unique reach, how much your channels overlap, and average frequency, plus a frequency distribution that flags who's being over-exposed and ready for a frequency cap.

It also connects spend to audiences: which audience each resolved customer joined on each channel, and every running audience's size, matched count, and match rate. Channel quirks are handled, not hidden - walled-garden social returns click and page-visit events only, while programmatic platforms pass both impressions and clicks, so unique people are counted whether or not they clicked.
3. Customer Journey
One chronological timeline of every interaction, site tag, server-side, channel logs, and in-store purchases, all unified under a single customer. Each touchpoint shows its type and the credit it earned, and when the same conversion arrives from both the tag and the server, it's de-duplicated automatically. Anonymous, pre-login activity is folded back into the customer's journey the moment they sign in.
Why it matters Today, attribution mostly means letting each platform grade its own homework: every channel reports its own conversions and takes full credit, so one shared sale gets claimed on Meta, on Search, and on The Trade Desk at once, and the totals overstate what really happened. Attribution & Value replaces that with one de-duplicated source of truth: each conversion is counted once, credit is split across the touchpoints that earned it, and every channel's claim is reconciled against a model whose exact configuration is versioned behind each run - no black box.
